title: Zephyrine and the Escarpment
premise: Coral Voss, a salvage diver haunted by a past he outruns port by port, is hired to strip a wreck the navy officially denies exists. When a government survey team vanishes on the escarpment above the coast—leaving intact gear, no bodies, and no tracks—he finds a survivor's journal that names him in its final pages. Pursued by the navy unit that erased the survey team and guided by Zephyrine, a cartographer's daughter who knows the range's hidden passes, Coral must cross the escarpment before the snows close it, discovering along the way that his own disappearance years ago was part of the same cover-up. In the end he chooses to stand and expose the truth rather than vanish again, finding belonging with Zephyrine at the cost of the only life he knew how to live.
about_author: Odile Ishikawa is a former marine surveyor who spent a decade mapping coastlines from Hokkaido to the Hebrides before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people who mistake motion for freedom.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Diving a wreck off a gray coastal town, Coral recovers sealed crates stamped with a government mark he recognizes and burns. The harbor master pays too well and asks nothing. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine—the first hint that this job is different.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral repairs his boat, the Kestrel, and deflects the town's friendly innkeeper, showing how deliberately he stays unmoored. A navy patrol boat circles the bay twice. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor; readers see the cost of his drifting.

chapters.title: Zephyrine
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A woman arrives asking passage upcoast: Zephyrine Marchand, carrying her missing father's survey maps. She knows things about the wreck she shouldn't. Coral refuses her; she waits anyway. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity—someone sees through him for the first time in years.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Up
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A storm shifts the wreck, exposing a compartment with a survey team's logbook—and photographs of an inland facility. One photo includes a younger Coral. Emotional beat: dread; his buried past surfaces literally.

chapters.title: The Vanished Survey
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Zephyrine explains her father's team vanished on the escarpment three weeks ago; authorities called it weather. Her maps mark a route no official chart shows. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into purpose; two searches become one.

chapters.title: Navy Men at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Navy officers board the Kestrel, confiscate the crates, and warn Coral away from 'restricted waters.' They mention his old name. Emotional beat: fear curdling into defiance—they've been hunting him longer than he knew.

chapters.title: Cutting Loose
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral slips out of harbor at night with Zephyrine hidden aboard, abandoning the salvage fee and his anonymity in one stroke. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror of commitment; running has finally become choosing.

chapters.title: The Last Harbor
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. They land at a decaying fishing village where Zephyrine's father once resupplied. An old friend of his gives them supplies and a warning: the navy bought the whole valley last spring. Emotional beat: warmth of borrowed community, shadowed by conspiracy.

chapters.title: Foot of the Escarpment
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The pair begins the climb through pine forest, following the hidden route on Marchand's map. Coral's diving-honed endurance is tested; Zephyrine proves the stronger navigator. Emotional beat: grudging respect turning toward trust.

chapters.title: The First Pass
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. They cross a knife-edge ridge as weather turns, finding a cairn her father built—freshly restacked. Someone alive has passed recently. Emotional beat: hope rekindled against mounting cold.

chapters.title: Signals in the Snow
chapters.summary: POV Coral. They find the survey camp: gear intact, tents pitched, meals half-eaten, no tracks leading out. Coral recognizes the navy's extraction methods. Emotional beat: horror—the team didn't die here; they were taken.

chapters.title: Marchand's Journal
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Hidden in the camp stove, her father's journal details the facility inland and ends with a page naming Coral Voss as 'the witness who escaped.' Emotional beat: betrayal and revelation—her search and his flight were always the same story.

chapters.title: Confrontation Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Zephyrine demands the truth; Coral confesses what he saw years ago aboard a navy transport and why he ran. Fury, then a fragile truce: they need each other. Emotional beat: intimacy forged through honesty; love begins here.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Ridge
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A navy tracking party spots their fire; a night chase across scree fields follows. Coral doubles back to mislead them, nearly dying in a crevasse Zephyrine talks him out of by voice alone. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into devotion.

chapters.title: The Shepherd's Bothy
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Sheltering in an abandoned bothy, they treat wounds and find evidence others have used it as a refuge from the valley below—a small history of the disappeared. Emotional beat: tenderness and resolve; they are not the first, and will not be the last.

chapters.title: The High Col
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The final pass must be crossed before an early storm seals it. They climb through the night, Zephyrine collapsing near the summit; Coral carries her over. Emotional beat: sacrifice made freely—the drifter becomes someone who stays.

chapters.title: Descent into the Valley
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Below the col lies the facility: a listening station cataloguing civilians, including the vanished survey team, held as 'security assets.' They spot Marchand alive at a window. Emotional beat: cold clarity of purpose; rescue now outweighs escape.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Escaped
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Using his old credentials and knowledge of navy procedure, Coral infiltrates the station while Zephyrine cuts the power line. He reaches Marchand's cell. Emotional beat: the past weaponized at last—everything he ran from becomes his tool.

chapters.title: Alarm
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The breakout goes wrong; alarms, floodlights, a standoff in the generator yard. Coral surrenders himself so Marchand and Zephyrine can reach the treeline. Emotional beat: climax of self-giving love against every survival instinct.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Facing the officer who erased his past, Coral reveals he copied the station's records during the infiltration—hidden where the navy can't retrieve them. Negotiation, not rescue, saves him. Emotional beat: power reversed; silence traded for testimony.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. With snow closing the passes behind them, the three descend the eastern route, escorting freed survey members. News of the records reaches the outside world. Emotional beat: exhaustion and release; the running finally stops.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Spring. Coral testifies, then returns to the coast town that once asked nothing of him—and this time stays. He and Zephyrine chart the escarpment together, putting the hidden route on every map. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, identity reclaimed, love settled into home.
